status_reason: A provisional assessment is possible using NIR diffuse reflection and MIR-ATR as screening-passed options for concentrated, opaque milk products, pending confirmation of exact optical properties and installation details.

premise_checks.premise: An initial spectroscopy concept and a practical comparison experiment can be provided while retaining laboratory checks.
premise_checks.explanation: Supplied materials demonstrate that multi-method laboratory trials and comparison experiments support industrial process monitoring while retaining laboratory reference checks.

citations.quote: having both fiber optic techniques available in a lab rather than relying on one provides the flexibility needed to monitor the entire production chain.

requirements_stated: Earlier information about fat and protein composition changes
In-line measurement in a flowing, opaque, concentrated milk product
Handling varying product temperature and texture during production
Practical comparison experiment while retaining laboratory checks

Required measurement accuracy and precision for fat and protein

recommendations.rationale: NIR diffuse reflection is well-suited for opaque, concentrated dairy streams and handles scattering media effectively.

citations.quote: NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.

recommendations.rationale: MIR-ATR provides high chemical selectivity and distinct functional group absorption bands for fat and protein components.
recommendations.conditions: To be tested if NIR scatter sensitivity proves too sensitive to texture variations.

citations.quote: ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples, such as biological tissue, using specialized probes utilizing high-transmission fiber optics in the Mid-IR region.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: Flush-mounted NIR diffuse reflection fiber probe or MIR-ATR immersion probe
measurement_concept.location: In-line in the processing line handling the concentrated milk product
measurement_concept.fiber_link: Robust fiber optic cables connecting the process probe to spectrometers located safely away from the processing floor

citations.quote: The use of fiber optics is critical here, as it allows the sensitive spectrometers to be located safely away from the vibration and dust of the manufacturing floor.
the probe is flush-mounted into a pipe or vat to interact directly with the flowing medium.

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal range 780-2500 nm; usable range depends on the instrument, fiber, and probe configuration.

citations.quote: NIR spectra (780-2500 nm) contain predominantly overtones and component bands of fundamental vibrations of molecules and atomic groups

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal range 4000-400 cm-1; usable range depends on the fiber and ATR crystal configuration.

citations.quote: Vibrational spectroscopy in the mid-IR range (4000-400 cm-1) is one of the most informative methods of chemical analysis.

risks.risk: Surface deposition or fouling on the probe tip can distort reflection and ATR signals in concentrated dairy products.

citations.quote: typically at a depth of few microns

risks.risk: Physical variations such as fat globule size and texture changes can mimic compositional changes in diffuse reflection measurements.

citations.quote: the method is sensitive to the surface characteristics and fat globule size.

chemometrics_note: Multivariate calibration (PLS) using scatter correction such as Standard Normal Variate (SNV) is required to remove physical scattering interference caused by texture and fat globule size variations.
realtime_tracking_note: In-line fiber optic probes enable real-time tracking of fat and protein composition changes directly in the flowing processing line.

proposal.what_would_change_it: Feasibility trial results showing insufficient prediction accuracy or robustness to texture changes with NIR alone.
proposal.next_step: Conduct multi-method laboratory trials using representative concentrated milk samples across expected temperature and texture ranges.

brief_answer: To monitor fat and protein in your concentrated milk product, we recommend testing NIR diffuse reflection as the primary in-line method, with MIR-ATR as a comparison. A practical comparison experiment using representative samples with varying temperature and texture should be conducted alongside your laboratory checks.
